results.name: all_even_set_odd_target_yes
results.description: Among multi-example sets whose examples are all even, yes rate for odd targets; observed above null means people break parity (endorse odd numbers after even examples) more than the model predicts, below means the model over-predicts parity violations.
results.code:
# name: all_even_set_odd_target_yes
# description: Among multi-example sets whose examples are all even, yes rate for odd targets; observed above null means people break parity (endorse odd numbers after even examples) more than the model predicts, below means the model over-predicts parity violations.
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    uniq = pd.unique(sets)
    codes = pd.Categorical(sets, categories=uniq).codes
    table = np.full((len(uniq), 4), np.nan)
    for i, s in enumerate(uniq):
        v = [int(x) for x in s.split(",")][:4]
        table[i, :len(v)] = v
    ex = table[codes]
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    alleven = np.all(np.isnan(ex) | (np.mod(ex, 2) == 0), axis=1) & (n > 1)
    m = alleven & (np.mod(t, 2) == 1)
    return float(y[m].mean()) if m.any() else 0.0

results.name: set_total_rejection_rate
results.description: Fraction of distinct sets (with 10+ responses) on which no target ever received a yes; observed above null means people reject all probes of some sets wholesale more often than the model predicts, below means the model predicts more all-no sets than observed.
results.code:
# name: set_total_rejection_rate
# description: Fraction of distinct sets (with 10+ responses) on which no target ever received a yes; observed above null means people reject all probes of some sets wholesale more often than the model predicts, below means the model predicts more all-no sets than observed.
def test_statistic(df):
    g = df["rating"].astype(float).groupby(df["number_set"].astype(str))
    cnt = g.size()
    s = g.sum()[cnt >= 10]
    return float((s == 0).mean()) if len(s) else 0.0

results.name: shared_units_digit_match_yes
results.description: Among sets of 2+ examples that all end in the same units digit, yes rate for non-example targets ending in that digit; observed below null means people extend 'ends in d' rules less than the model predicts, above means more.
results.code:
# name: shared_units_digit_match_yes
# description: Among sets of 2+ examples that all end in the same units digit, yes rate for non-example targets ending in that digit; observed below null means people extend 'ends in d' rules less than the model predicts, above means more.
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    uniq = pd.unique(sets)
    codes = pd.Categorical(sets, categories=uniq).codes
    table = np.full((len(uniq), 4), np.nan)
    for i, s in enumerate(uniq):
        v = [int(x) for x in s.split(",")][:4]
        table[i, :len(v)] = v
    ex = table[codes]
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    u = np.mod(ex, 10)
    u0 = u[:, 0]
    same = np.all(np.isnan(ex) | (u == u0[:, None]), axis=1) & (n > 1)
    notin = ~np.any(ex == t[:, None], axis=1)
    m = same & notin & (np.mod(t, 10) == u0)
    return float(y[m].mean()) if m.any() else 0.0

results.name: cell_response_variance
results.description: Mean within-cell Bernoulli variance p(1-p) of yes responses across repeated (set, target) cells with 5+ responses; observed above null means people disagree on the same item more than the model's predicted probabilities imply (model too extreme/confident), below means people are more unanimous than the model predicts.
results.code:
# name: cell_response_variance
# description: Mean within-cell Bernoulli variance p(1-p) of yes responses across repeated (set, target) cells with 5+ responses; observed above null means people disagree on the same item more than the model's predicted probabilities imply (model too extreme/confident), below means people are more unanimous than the model predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    key = df["number_set"].astype(str) + "|" + df["target"].astype(str)
    g = df["rating"].astype(float).groupby(key)
    cnt = g.size()
    p = g.mean()[cnt >= 5]
    return float((p * (1 - p)).mean()) if len(p) else 0.0

results.name: all_odd_set_parity_contrast
results.description: Among multi-example sets whose examples are all odd, yes rate for odd targets minus yes rate for even targets (targets not in the set); observed below null means people generalise parity from all-odd sets less than the model predicts (model over-weights the 'odd' rule), above means more.
results.code:
# name: all_odd_set_parity_contrast
# description: Among multi-example sets whose examples are all odd, yes rate for odd targets minus yes rate for even targets (targets not in the set); observed below null means people generalise parity from all-odd sets less than the model predicts (model over-weights the 'odd' rule), above means more.
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    uniq = pd.unique(sets)
    codes = pd.Categorical(sets, categories=uniq).codes
    table = np.full((len(uniq), 4), np.nan)
    for i, s in enumerate(uniq):
        v = [int(x) for x in s.split(",")][:4]
        table[i, :len(v)] = v
    ex = table[codes]
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    allodd = np.all(np.isnan(ex) | (np.mod(ex, 2) == 1), axis=1) & (n > 1)
    notin = ~np.any(ex == t[:, None], axis=1)
    a = allodd & notin & (np.mod(t, 2) == 1)
    b = allodd & notin & (np.mod(t, 2) == 0)
    if not a.any() or not b.any():
        return 0.0
    return float(y[a].mean() - y[b].mean())

results.name: multi_example_proximity_gradient
results.description: On sets of 2+ examples, yes rate for non-example targets within 3 of the nearest example minus yes rate for targets 15+ away from every example; observed above null means people generalise by numeric proximity more than the model predicts, below means less (people less similarity-driven than the model's ranges).
results.code:
# name: multi_example_proximity_gradient
# description: On sets of 2+ examples, yes rate for non-example targets within 3 of the nearest example minus yes rate for targets 15+ away from every example; observed above null means people generalise by numeric proximity more than the model predicts, below means less (people less similarity-driven than the model's ranges).
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    uniq = pd.unique(sets)
    codes = pd.Categorical(sets, categories=uniq).codes
    table = np.full((len(uniq), 4), np.nan)
    for i, s in enumerate(uniq):
        v = [int(x) for x in s.split(",")][:4]
        table[i, :len(v)] = v
    ex = table[codes]
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    d = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    a = (n > 1) & (d >= 1) & (d <= 3)
    b = (n > 1) & (d >= 15)
    if not a.any() or not b.any():
        return 0.0
    return float(y[a].mean() - y[b].mean())
